title: How does a new memory become one that lasts?

cards.title: A brand-new memory is like wet cement: soft at first
cards.text: A memory is a set of brain cells that fired together during an experience, now linked so they can fire together again. But a brand-new memory is like wet cement: it's soft at first, and it needs time to set.
cards.hook: So what does it take for a memory to set?

notes: A few brain cells light up together, then stay linked
The linked cells sit in soft wet cement that has not set yet

cards.title: Within hours, the cells build proteins that make their links sturdier
cards.text: Turning it into a memory that lasts is called consolidation. Within hours, those cells build new proteins, the building material that makes their links sturdier.

notes: Two linked brain cells, a thin link between them
Proteins travel to the link and it grows thick

cards.title: The hippocampus ties the pieces together into one memory
cards.text: A memory has pieces: what you saw, heard and felt, each kept in a different part of your brain. The hippocampus, a seahorse-shaped part deep in your brain, ties those pieces together into one memory.
cards.hook: So what does the hippocampus do while you sleep?

notes: What you saw, heard and felt land in three parts of a brain
A seahorse-shaped hippocampus deep inside ties them together

cards.title: In deep sleep, the hippocampus replays your day to the cortex
cards.text: In deep sleep, the hippocampus replays your day to the cortex, the brain's outer layer, gradually moving it into long-term storage.

notes: A sleeping brain under a moon
Replays flow from the hippocampus to the outer layer, which holds the memory

cards.title: Students who sleep after studying remember more than those who pull an all-nighter
cards.text: Studies show that students who sleep after studying remember more than students who pull an all-nighter. Learning doesn't end when you close the book.
cards.takeaway: A new memory starts soft, its cells build proteins, the hippocampus ties its pieces together, and sleep moves it into long-term storage.

notes: A student asleep and a student pulling an all-nighter
Recap: soft cement, links thickening, the hippocampus tying pieces, sleep replay to the cortex

cards.note: Each time you recall a memory, it can soften again for a while and has to set again.
